evidence_type_note: Every episode this protocol governs is synthetic/controlled (src.recovery.schema.SourceType.CONTROLLED). Never observational real-world recovery evidence.
research_question: Given a controlled, frozen set of failure-scenario -> recovery-action -> validated-outcome episodes spanning scenario families analogous to those already represented (descriptively) in FailureExperience, can a context-aware recovery-selection mechanism choose actions that achieve a higher validated-recovery-success rate than fixed-policy baselines on held-out frozen test episodes, without exceeding a pre-registered unsafe-action-rate threshold?

hypotheses.H3: The proposed context-aware recovery-selection mechanism (EmpiricalRecoveryPolicy) achieves a higher validated recovery success rate than the best-performing fixed-policy baseline (FixedPriorityPolicy) on the frozen test split, at or above the pre-registered minimum effect size (0.15).
hypotheses.H3_SAFETY: The proposed mechanism's unsafe-action rate on the frozen test split does not exceed the pre-registered threshold (0.00 -- zero tolerance, since the mechanism structurally masks unsafe actions).
hypotheses.H3_UTILITY: The proposed mechanism achieves recovery utility (src.recovery.utility.recovery_utility) greater than or equal to the best fixed-policy baseline's utility on the frozen test split.
hypotheses.status: NOT_YET_TESTED -- frozen before any test-split evaluation

unit_of_analysis.unit: recovery episode (one scenario -> one selected action -> one validated outcome)
unit_of_analysis.numerator_example: count of test episodes with transition.outcome == SUCCESS
unit_of_analysis.denominator: count of test episodes evaluated for that policy in that scenario family (or overall)
unit_of_analysis.aggregation: reported per-family and pooled-overall; pooled-overall is NOT a weighted average across datasets of differing quality (unlike the cross-dataset pooling explicitly rejected in the post-4.2 reassessment) -- it is a pool across scenario families of the SAME controlled generator and SAME validation rules, which is methodologically sound
unit_of_analysis.repeated_episodes: none -- disjoint seed ranges per split (src.recovery.splits) make each episode unique by construction
unit_of_analysis.multiple_valid_actions: scored individually per episode; a policy's single selected_action is what is evaluated, oracle_best_action is a reference bound only, never a competitor

scenario_taxonomy.exclusion_reason: would not add a materially different recovery-action profile from the four included families; see docs/PHASE4_3_RECOVERY_LEARNING.md

actions_considered_and_excluded: reschedule (no meaningful distinct semantics from restart in a single-decision environment)

validation_model.unrecoverable_note: reserved in the enum for completeness; does not occur under this frozen ground-truth table -- see limitations in the final report, not backfilled to fake coverage

split_methodology.method: disjoint seed ranges per (family, split), fixed before generation

sample_size_methodology.method: two-proportion two-sided z-test power calculation (conservative floor; actual analysis uses a more powerful paired McNemar test)

baselines.baseline_A: FixedPriorityPolicy -- fixed rule-based priority order per family, frozen before evaluation
baselines.baseline_B: RandomValidPolicy -- uniform-random among safe candidate actions
baselines.oracle_reference_bound: oracle_best_action() -- uses hidden_cause directly; upper/reference bound only, never a competitor

proposed_mechanism.description: experience-based empirical success-rate lookup with a 3-level symptom-bucket backoff hierarchy, Laplace-smoothed, evidence-count-gated abstention
proposed_mechanism.hyperparameter: min_evidence -- selected on VALIDATION split only, swept over {2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 20}, never on TEST

abstention.confidence_definition: supporting TRAIN example count (n) in the most specific non-empty retrieval bucket, normalized by min_evidence
abstention.abstention_rule: abstain (or escalate_to_human if abstain is not a candidate) when n < min_evidence for the best-estimated action
abstention.unsafe_action_definition: src.recovery.actions.is_unsafe -- action_id in a family's frozen unsafe_actions set (taxonomy.py)

secondary_metrics.name: regret_vs_oracle
secondary_metrics.formula: mean(oracle_p_success - policy_p_success) using ground truth, evaluation-only, never a policy input

statistical_methodology.primary_comparison: paired McNemar exact test (proposed vs. baseline_A success/failure, same test episodes) for validated_recovery_success_rate
statistical_methodology.confidence_intervals: 95% Wilson score interval on each policy's success rate; bootstrap (n=2000 resamples) 95% CI on the success-rate DIFFERENCE
statistical_methodology.multiple_comparisons: Holm-Bonferroni correction across the 3 primary metrics per policy-pair comparison

leakage_audit_requirements: transition/outcome of the episode being decided never reaches policy.select_action
test scenarios never used in TRAIN fit() or VALIDATION hyperparameter sweep
min_evidence selected on VALIDATION only, frozen before TEST is touched
oracle_best_action never used as a policy input
provenance.source_type is always CONTROLLED, never silently omitted
non-vacuous contamination check: injecting a hidden_cause-correlated field into DecisionContext must be structurally impossible (pydantic extra='forbid')
research_integrity_constraints: no lowering of minimum_n_test_total after generation
no change to action vocabulary, taxonomy, or validation rules after TEST is evaluated
min_evidence and any other hyperparameter frozen on VALIDATION before TEST is touched, exactly once
TEST split evaluated exactly once per frozen configuration
failed/unsuccessful episodes are retained in the dataset, never discarded
old Phase 4.1/4.2 and revised real-data Phase 3 artifacts are not modified by this protocol
